kids.content: What We Did On Our Holiday

10.50pm BBC2 (Andy Hamilton, Guy Jenkin, 2014) A sweet domestic comedy from the makers of the sitcom Outnumbered, viewed from the children’s focus but involving the divorce of parents Rosamund Pike and David Tennant and death of granddad Billy Connolly.

9pm, TCM (George Miller, 1979) In the taut little exploitation ﬂick that made him a star, Mel Gibson plays a cop patrolling the highways of a post-apocalyptic future in a supercharged Ford Falcon GT, and grimly chasing down a biker gang with revenge in mind.

Billy, might wonder where the sweetness lay. Annual seaside holidays in Rothesay provides one of his Proustian memories in this concluding half of his memoir, along with knitted woolly swimming trunks and “the poetry of swearing”.

9pm, Channel 4 Following Christmas Eve’s Big Fat Quiz Of The Year, celebrity question-setters Jon Snow and Charles Dance (among others) tickle the much wider general knowledge of Sandi Toksvig – her QI training coming in handy here – Joe Lycett, Katherine Ryan, David Baddiel, Frank Skinner and Big Narstie. Jimmy Carr asks questions that range from Polish ﬁlm titles to Digger the Crab.

9pm, More4 (Martin Scorsese, 2013) Scorsese’s 21st feature ﬁlm is adapted from an unrepentant tell-all memoir by Jordan Belfort (played by Leonardo DiCaprio, left), a cocksure but legally shady and morally repugnant founder of an upstart brokerage ﬁrm, who, before he was eventually brought low by an FBI investigation in the late 90s, amassed more wealth than Croesus would have known what to do with. It is an exhilarating, exhausting three-hour audiovisual bacchanalia of obscene conspicuous consumption, prostitutes and strippers, yachts and helicopters, drugs, sex and more drugs. And it is late-period Scorsese’s ﬂashiest, funniest work by some margin.
